# Blind RSA / Privacy Pass type 0x0002 test vectors (Phase 8 design §2.9): one file, several replayers.
#
# Format: '#' starts a comment; '[name]' starts a section; 'vector <id> [description]' starts a
# vector; 'key = hex' (the value may be empty) is a field of the current vector. Hex is lowercase and
# joined across the RFC's line wraps; nothing in the RFC sections is recomputed.
#
# [rfc9474-a]  RFC 9474 "RSA Blind Signatures", Appendix A "Test Vectors",
#              https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9474.txt (retrieved 2026-09-12):
#              A.1 RSABSSA-SHA384-PSS-Randomized and A.3 RSABSSA-SHA384-PSS-Deterministic (the two
#              48-byte-salt variants; A.2 and A.4 are PSSZERO, which GHOST does not use). The modulus
#              is 4096-bit. Replayed through the generic raw functions of ghost-blind-rsa
#              (emsa_pss_encode_sha384 over prepared_msg, blind_raw, finalize_raw, verify via ring) and
#              directly through blind-rsa-signatures =0.17.2 (its blind signature must equal
#              blind_sig): issuer/crates/blind-rsa/tests/rfc9474_vectors.rs. Neither the production
#              Signer (256-byte blocks) nor the ES parser (2048-bit keys) replays this section.
#
# [rfc9578-a2] RFC 9578 "Privacy Pass Issuance Protocols", Appendix A.2 "Issuance Protocol 2 - Blind
#              RSA (2048-bit)", all 5 vectors, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9578.txt (retrieved
#              2026-09-12). skI is the hex of a PEM PKCS #8 private key; pkI the RSASSA-PSS SPKI;
#              token_request = token_type(2) || truncated_token_key_id(1) || blinded_msg(256);
#              token_response = blind_sig(256). Replayed through the production type-0x0002 path of
#              ghost-entitlement (key id, challenge parse, token parse, blind, finalize, verify):
#              issuer/crates/entitlement/tests/rfc9578_vectors.rs, and through the production issuer
#              Signer (the RFC evidence for it): issuer/crates/service/tests/signer.rs.
#
# [ghost]      GHOST-specific vectors produced by this implementation (regression pins, not RFC
#              evidence): redemption contexts, challenge encodings per kind, key ids, nullifiers,
#              permutation proofs (valid and tampered), seed-derived batch positions, layout and
#              request digests over the test Entitlement Schedule
#              (issuer/crates/entitlement/tests/fixtures/test_schedule.ghes).
#
# [perm-proof-negative] Keys the permutation-proof verifier must refuse although their proof is
#              mathematically valid (design §3.1 rule 2, §3.2). small-factor-65537: n = f * p * q
#              with f = 65537 and 65537 dividing none of f - 1, p - 1, q - 1, so x -> x^e permutes
#              Z_n^* and proof = σ_0..σ_7 (σ_i = ρ_i^d mod n) verifies; only the trial division
#              "no prime factor <= 65 537" refuses the key. Regenerated deterministically and
#              compared by issuer/crates/blind-rsa/tests/permutation_proof.rs; replayed as the ES
#              case key-small-factor by issuer/crates/entitlement/tests/schedule_vectors.rs.
